study type: Secondary analysis of a multicenter prospective study
outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of prenatal ultrasound for posterior PAS
Surgical outcome (placenta accreta, increta, percreta, hysterectomy, balloon tamponade insertion)
cohort: The study included 258 patients aged >=18 years with a posterior low-lying placenta (<20 mm from the internal cervical os) or placenta previa (covering the os), undergoing ultrasound assessment at >=26(+0) weeks of gestation across 16 referral hospitals.
finding: Prior uterine surgery, specifically prior C-sections and myomectomy with uterine penetration, are common risk factors for posterior PAS in patients with placenta previa or low-lying placenta, and posterior PAS is associated with a lower risk of hysterectomy compared to anterior PAS.
